0434a411803905bad418971f437d75694530be03.summary: SentinelOne research on FIN7, a financially motivated group active since 2012 with origins in Russia. It links several underground forum sellers of AV-killer tools to FIN7 and describes AvNeutralizer, which uses a newly seen driver-based method to tamper with security products. It also covers automated SQL injection and Exchange exploitation via the Checkmarks platform, plus Powertrash loaders, Diceloader, Core Impact implants and an SSH-based backdoor. Several attributions are hedged at high or medium confidence.

hedges: Sellers goodsoft, lefroggy, killerAV and Stupor assessed with high confidence as belonging to the FIN7 cluster, likely using multiple pseudonyms to mask identity.
Cannot conclusively determine whether LockBit intrusions involving AvNeutralizer were executed by FIN7; no direct evidence links them to the group.
One RSA key attributed to FIN7 with medium confidence; loaders showed overlapping configurations.
Automated SQL injection intrusions attributed to FIN7 and the Auto-SQLi module with medium confidence.
Report hypothesizes AvNeutralizer was likely sold on criminal forums, with Black Basta as one of the early buyers.
Suspected that the SSH-based backdoor intrusion aimed at covert persistent access for future espionage; a suspicion, not a confirmed finding.
